calendar_reminder_surface_label: Example State official voter-information calendar/reminder surface policy
delivery_role_note: Calendar subscriptions, .ics downloads, and similar reminder artifacts may help voters remember dates, but they do not become the controlling authority for jurisdiction-specific election rules.
authority_boundary_note: The current official calendar page, signed notice, or direct office confirmation remains controlling even when a voter carries forward an imported or subscribed calendar object.
subscription_calendar_policy_note: If the jurisdiction publishes a subscription calendar, the linked official page should explain scope, refresh expectations, and where superseding notices appear.
downloadable_ics_policy_note: If the jurisdiction offers a downloadable .ics file, treat it as an optional convenience artifact with clear scope labeling and a visible path back to the current official page.
event_card_policy_note: Machine-readable event/date representations should point back to a durable current official page rather than trying to act as a complete standalone rule source.
timezone_policy_note: Timed election-service windows should state local-time semantics clearly and avoid pseudo-UTC or ambiguous offsets that can shift voter action.
all_day_vs_timed_policy_note: All-day civic dates and timed office/service windows should be represented differently so reminders do not silently reinterpret one as the other.
recurrence_rollover_policy_note: Recurring or subscription-style calendar artifacts should make cycle rollover and supersession explicit instead of looking evergreen by default.
calendar_link_disclosure_note: Calendar download or subscription actions should be labeled as non-HTML handoffs rather than being presented as if they were ordinary page navigation.
current_state_recovery_policy_note: Linked landing pages should recover safely from stale reminders by exposing current-state cues and immediate routes to the current notice/help lane.
